spans.s: Ākāśa-Gaṅgā (“the heavenly Gaṅgā”). § 11 (Parvas.). I, 1, 638.--§ 421 (Gandhamādanaprav.): III, 142, 10909: In the neighbourhood of the Mandara mountain, the abode of the gods and ṛshis; coming from Badarī, honoured by Vaihāyasas and Vālakhilyas and Gandharvas and singers of Sāmans; there Marīci, Pulaha, Bhṛgu, and Aṅgiras, with the host of M., mutter their daily prayers; S., A., the Moon, the Sun, the stars, and planets circumambulate it; Śiva (Vṛshāṅkah) carries its water on his head at Gangādvāra. According to the counsel of Lomaśa the Pāṇḍavas adored it, and then continued their journey with the hosts of ṛshis.-§ 714 (Śukakṛtya): XII, 389, 12410.--§ 717b (Nārāyaṇīya): XII, 343, ††13218 VIII).--§ 795 (Svargārohanap.): XVIII, 3, 108.

Akampana(ḥ), a king. § 594 (Abhimanyuv.): VII, 52, 2023, 2029; 54, 2125: In days of old there was a king named Akampana. Once, on the field of battle, he was surrounded by his foes. His son Hari was at last slain in the midst of the army. A. grieved day and night. Then the D.-ṛ. Nārada came and told him the origin of death (Mṛtyu, q.v.). “Therefore,” said Nārada, “don't indulge in fruitless grief for creatures after they are dead…” Akampana felt consoled, and Nārada went to the woods of Nandana.
Akāra (“the letter a”): VI, 1237 (aksharāṇām akāro 'smi, says Kṛshṇa about himself).
Ākarsha. § 287 (Rājasūyikap.): II, 34, 1270 (among the kings who came to Yudhishṭhira's rājasūya).
